corrected.reason: Commander battlesuits take drones. Upstream lists neither the abilities nor the wargear budget, so a Commander's Gun Drone was dropped on import — its twin pulse carbine missing from the shooting table and its Shield Drone missing from the rules. Evidenced by a validated War Organ export of a legal 2,000 point list.

Drones as for the Enforcer Commander. The Shield Generator is a separate problem: upstream lists it BOTH as a standard ability and as a wargear option, so the app could not tell whether a list that never mentions buying one has a 4+ invulnerable save. Treated as standard, which is what the ability list implies and what makes the statline agree with the rules text. If a Coldstar has to pay for its Shield Generator, this entry is the thing to change.
Crisis Starscythe suits take the same drones as Crisis Fireknife suits, whose datasheet does list them. The omission looks like a transcription slip rather than a rule.
Broadsides take Missile Drones. The ability exists and is attached to the Riptide, but not here.
The Ghostkeel takes a Battlesuit Support System. The ability exists and is attached to other battlesuits, but not to this one.
Stealth Battlesuits take a Gun Drone and a Marker Drone. Both abilities exist in the faction data; neither is attached to this datasheet.
The Gun Drone's gun. Pointing the grant at the plain `twin-pulse-carbine` had the drone firing at BS4+, the skill of the battlesuit carrying it, which is a better weapon than the drone has.

The MV15 Gun Drone's gun, carried by The Twin Lance. Upstream names it only as free text — "twin pulse blaster" — with no record to resolve. Written out rather than derived: the profile confirmed against the datasheet is 12" with TWIN LINKED, where upstream's `pulse-blaster` is 10" without it, so this is not simply its namesake at BS5+.

The Missile Drone's gun: a missile pod at BS5+. Upstream records the drone as granting `{grant_type: ranged-weapon}` with no weapon named and has no record for it either, so Broadsides and Riptides were fielding drones that shot nothing.

autoreactive-camouflage-advanced-acquisi.name: Autoreactive Camouflage
autoreactive-camouflage-advanced-acquisi.community_notes: [APPROX] When a hidden PATHFINDER TEAM or STEALTH BATTLESUITS unit is targeted in your opponent's Shooting phase, it gets +1 to its Save characteristic. The 'hidden' precondition is not gated here. Full rule in raw-text store.

corrected.reason: A Gun Drone brings a twin pulse carbine. Upstream records only `{grant_type: ranged-weapon}` with no weapon named, so the app could say "grants a ranged weapon" and nothing more — no profile, no attacks, and nothing in the shooting table. The Recon Drone in the same file shows the intended shape, with an explicit weapon_id.

While the Commander leads a unit, the whole squad's ranged weapons gain ASSAULT as well as moving 12". Upstream carries only the Move part, so the app showed a mobility buff and said nothing about being able to shoot after Advancing — which is the reason to take the detachment.
The AP improvement does not apply against VEHICLE or MONSTER targets. Upstream has no restriction, so the app promised -1 AP against exactly the targets where it does not help.
Names the weapon by id rather than as free text, so the grant resolves to a profile the shooting table can show.

Advanced Armour is Feel No Pain 4+ against mortal wounds only. The upstream effect has no qualifier, so the app rendered an unrestricted Feel No Pain 4+ — a much stronger ability than the Broadside has, and exactly the kind of confidently wrong number that loses games.
Names the weapon the drone brings, as the Recon Drone already does. Without a weapon_id the grant is unresolvable and the drone's shots never reach the table.

In 11th edition Stealth gives the unit the Benefit of Cover. Upstream still carries the 10th edition rule, -1 to the attacker's Hit roll, in all three faction files. Reported by the app's user against the current rulebook. The two are not interchangeable: cover changes the save, a hit penalty changes the roll, and they stack differently with everything else on the table.
